entries.name: Godot demo projects

licensing.asset_license: Repository demos are distributed under the repository MIT licence; imported/externally substituted assets still require separate provenance.

fit.engine_or_stack: Godot 4.x; branch/version compatibility must match the target engine
platforms: mobile where the selected demo supports it

entries.notes: Official solved-system source for controllers, rendering, physics, navigation, UI and template patterns before bespoke Godot implementation. Select individual demos by exact path and re-check their asset provenance before production reuse.

entries.name: Dialogic 2

licensing.asset_license: Roboto may be used under Apache-2.0; project/game assets authored around Dialogic remain separate.

fit.engine_or_stack: Godot 4.3+ according to current upstream documentation
platforms: Godot-supported targets subject to project validation

entries.notes: Mature dialogue/visual-novel/character framework candidate. Upstream warns public APIs may change during alpha/beta, so production adoption still requires version pinning and project-level regression tests.

entries.name: OpenTTD

licensing.asset_license: Game/base-set content and third-party components have their own licence boundaries; inspect exact reused material.

entries.notes: High-value complete-game reference for simulation, networking, save/load, content/mod systems and long-lived operations. GPL-2.0 means it is not silently promoted as a proprietary drop-in component.

entries.name: Kenney game assets

licensing.asset_license: CC0/public domain on current Kenney asset pages; preserve exact asset-page provenance and included licence files.

entries.notes: Current Kenney support documentation says game assets on asset pages are CC0 and may be used commercially without attribution. Production intake must still record the exact pack URL/version/files rather than treating the mutable library homepage as immutable provenance.
